skill_draft.name: differential_diagnosis_unilateral_whiteout
skill_draft.description: When interpreting a chest X-ray showing unilateral hemithorax opacification (whiteout), the agent must differentiate between volume loss and volume gain mechanisms before concluding a diagnosis.
skill_draft.applicable_conditions: Any medical imaging interpretation task involving unilateral lung opacification, mediastinal shift, or complete hemithorax whiteout on chest radiography.
skill_draft.core_action: If a chest X-ray shows unilateral opacification: (1) Assess mediastinal position relative to the opacity (shift toward indicates volume loss like atelectasis/agenesis; shift away indicates volume gain like effusion/mass; central suggests consolidation); (2) Evaluate diaphragm position and rib spacing on the affected side; (3) Explicitly list differential diagnoses based on these volume indicators (e.g., massive atelectasis vs. pleural effusion vs. agenesis) before selecting the final diagnosis. Do not diagnose agenesis solely based on opacity without ruling out acquired causes of volume loss.
